Continue reading...
items.body:
The first Aaron Sorkin Facebook movie, 2010’s The Social Network, helped cement the early aughts image of Mark Zuckerberg rebelling against corporate norms in rumpled hoodies and T-shirts.
The follow-up, The Social Reckoning, is carbon-dated from 2019 to 2021. This is “post-hoodie”, as the movie’s costume designer, Susan Lyall, describes it, “post-thumbing his nose” to formality. It is also peak robot. Zuckerberg’s reserved wardrobe of suits or interchangeable long-sleeved shirts echo his chilling composure throughout, even as fury simmers under the surface.
The costume was based on deep research by Lyall and also by actor Jeremy Strong who, she says, is “very into costume”. Having worked together before, on the Sorkin movies Molly’s Game and The Trial of the Chicago 7, they would text a lot during the preparation process.
“He reaches out before I even get to reach out to him. It’s my third movie with him, so I’m pretty used to it. He’s very proactive. He’s one of my favourite actors because of that. He would know exactly where [Zuckerberg] wore what. He wanted the exact Nike shoe – the footwear was very important to him – and the exact Brunello Cucinelli T-shirt and sweater, and so on,” she says.
Strong has become notorious for method acting, and method dressing, too, seems to be part of his process. “It’s sort of the first step in the performance. That and the haircut,” says Lyall.
The conversations went deep. “It’s actually kind of nerdy, you know, to sit there and talk about the color of the shoelaces. There aren’t that many people who want to talk about that. I always joke with him, if the acting thing doesn’t work out, you can have a position in my department!” she says.
Lyall found those Nikes – to be specific, the 2018 Nike Flyknit trainer in black anthracite – on Grailed. For the sweaters, it was Strong, she says, who worked out how to reach the eye-wateringly expensive Italian luxury brand Brunello Cucinelli, in order to buy specific pieces, “because we don’t want the latest. We want stuff from five or six years ago, and they were very helpful at procuring it. And that was because of him. He was really proactive.”
Lyall has spent a lot of hours thinking about how tech oligarchs dress. Not only Zuckerberg but Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and others too, who were partial inspiration for another of her recent credits, the 2025 Jesse Armstrong movie Mountainhead about four devilish plutocrats.
They, too, wore a lot of Brunello Cucinelli. That brand sells cashmere cardigans for $16,500 and ribbed sweaters for $4,600. Amusingly, it currently has the Immanuel Kant quote “beauty is the symbol of the morally good” in prime place on its website homepage.
In Lyall’s view, Brunello Cucinelli is a “safety net for people like Mark Zuckerberg. If they’re not sure about what they’re wearing, if they pay a lot for it, they feel a little better about it. You know, if this little sweater is $2,000, it must be good. It’s kind of a security blanket, or just an affirmation of your own success. You’re going to be OK if you’re wearing this tasteful thing.”
The Zuckerberg of The Social Reckoning had moved on from the earlier antifashion stance that prompted him to declare, in 2014, that he was “not a cool person”, and only wore grey T-shirts because he wanted to make “as few decisions as possible … I feel like I’m not doing my job if I spend any of my energy on things that are silly or frivolous.”
By the period captured in the movie, says Lyall, “I believe Zuckerberg was trying to be relatable, but also starting to understand Silicon Valley’s obsession with taste and the cost of things.” He was also more buff than he had been. In her interpretation, he seemed to be thinking: “My fit physique looks very nice in this clingy but expensive sweater. And ‘if you know, you know’ – I think there’s a bit of that. But I also think, he’s nouveau riche without being gaudy. It’s not without taste.”
Since then, Zuckerberg’s outward presentation has graduated to outright peacocking.
For the tech billionaires, in general, says Lyall: “I think something happened. I think they have discovered a new way to flex. And it’s not quiet luxury. It’s loud.”
For Zuckerberg specifically – whose makeover came suddenly with ostentatious gold chains, Loewe shorts and Alexander McQueen suits embellished with dragonflies in around 2024 – it could not feel much more strategic.
Dabbling with fashion allows Zuckerberg to look like a different guy from the one we have seen so many times sweating in a suit in front of Congress. It also provides a distraction from the reality of his products and work, giving him something soft and harmless to talk about.
Zuckerberg has even used the classic fiction writer’s trick of embedding backstory within his jewellery. In 2024, when he started wearing a large, gold pendant necklace over his T-shirt, he claimed it wasn’t just because he wanted to look like a hip-hop star, as the internet understandably concluded.
When finally asked about his pendant in an interview (“oh this?” he said, with an approximation of spontaneity) he explained that it was embossed with a Jewish prayer he sings to his kids every night at bedtime, thus reminding the public of his humanity – his faith, and the importance he places on being there for his children.
This year, as Meta has recruited fashion stars such as Kylie Jenner to market its smart glasses, he has spent yet more time courting fashion, attending Prada shows and the Met Gala.
Last month, he gave the New York Times an interview purely about clothing, claiming that he buys almost all of his wardrobe on Instagram himself – which sounds extremely decision-requiring and time-consuming for a person of his workload.
Many of the labels he mentioned were more contemporary, less oligarch-coded, among them Mike Amiri, a purveyor of $400-ish T-shirts, with whom he has worked on bespoke items including the “Building is my love language” he wore to present Muse at a Facebook conference. Online, too, when he buys something of the $200-ish, rather than $2000-ish price tag, he may even pop into the comments, when complimented on that item, to draw users’ attention towards it (“It’s @johnelliottco – I’m loving their stuff recently”).
Just as the new personal AI assistant Muse has been fashioned to look utterly adorable – surely such a cute fluffy Labubu-like creature could never spark an apocalypse! – Zuckerberg’s own continuing makeover appears conceived to make him a more friendly and, ideally, more human.
In fashion, though, it’s not as simple as ticking the box to confirm you are not a robot. When he explained his interest in style to the New York Times, for example, he said, “I think the company is an instantiation of my values” and claimed he wanted to “be intentional about how I program that”.
A turn of phrase that suggests that, under his vibrant new clothing, the cashmere-clad machine depicted in Sorkin’s movie may not have been properly deactivated.

items.body:
Authentic Italian bakery giant Balconi is taking its UK expansion to the next level this autumn, announcing major nation-wide listings across Tesco and ASDA starting September, followed by further discounter expansion in October.
Balconi’s autumn expansion cements its position as a major player in the UK ambient cake aisle. Grounded in a rich 70-year heritage that began in a small pastry shop in Nerviano, Milan, the brand embodies Italy’s world-renowned reputation for exceptional culinary quality and uncompromising ingredients. Built on the belief that great baking starts with clean, simple recipes, Balconi crafts its authentic recipes using high-quality ingredients, free from artificial sweeteners, colourants, or preservatives, combining classic artisan tradition with modern baking to bring a genuine taste of la dolce vita to everyday moments.
Heading straight into major grocery aisles from early September:
Tesco Exclusive
- Italian White Chocolate Cake Rolls Milk: An indulgent new twist featuring soft sponge rolls filled with sweet milk cream and enrobed in a smooth white chocolate coating.
Tesco Launch
- Italian Cake Rolls Cocoa Cream 10-Packs: These iconic 10-pack sponge spirals offer triple cocoa goodness, rolled sponge, luscious filling, and a smooth cocoa shell in both rich Cocoa and Milk Cream options.
ASDA Launch
- Italian Wafer Cubes Hazelnut: Light, crispy, multi-layered wafer bites filled with a rich hazelnut cream, crafted without artificial colours, sweeteners or preservatives.
Wholesale Expansion
- Italian Sponge Slices Strawberry: Soft, fluffy cake slices filled with sweet, fruity strawberry, perfect for lunchboxes and on-the-go snacking.
Completing the nationwide rollout in early October, Balconi will also launch a standalone 6-pack of its bestselling Italian Cake Roll Cocoa across discounter stores.
Michael Inpong, chief marketing officer at Valeo Foods UK, said: “Entering Tesco and ASDA marks an incredible milestone in our UK journey as we dial up our passion for authentic Italian living across the country. In Italy, food is all about connection, warmth, and taking time out to enjoy a traditional afternoon “merenda”. Every bake that is produced carries over 70 years of Milanese pastry-making heritage, born from a small family shop near Milan”
“UK consumers are looking for high-quality, authentic sweet treats that bring a true taste of la dolce vita without compromising on value. By expanding our footprint with national supermarket partners and introducing exciting new innovations, like our White Chocolate Cake Rolls and Hazelnut Wafer Cubes, we are making the everyday joy and daily luxury of authentic Italian bakery accessible to millions more homes across the UK.”

items.body:
Abu Bakr Supermarkets managing director Hamza Hussain has been named a finalist in the Next Gen Award category at the prestigious Asian Trader Awards, adding to an impressive run of recognition for the young West Yorkshire business leader.
The managing director of the Batley-based supermarket group has been shortlisted among the next generation of talent shaping the UK convenience retail industry, following his recent success in the 30 Under 30 awards.
Hamza’s latest nomination recognises his contribution to the family-run business and his ambitions to build on its established presence in West Yorkshire while exploring opportunities for future growth.
The Asian Trader Awards are a major event in the UK convenience retail calendar, bringing together retailers, suppliers and industry leaders to celebrate achievement and innovation across the sector.
The winner of the Next Gen Award will be announced on November 4 at the Park Plaza Westminster Bridge in London, where industry figures will gather for the annual awards ceremony.
For Hamza, the latest shortlist comes at an important point in his career, following his recognition in the 30 Under 30 awards, which celebrate young talent making an impact across the industry.
Speaking about the latest recognition, Hamza Hussain said: “Being named a finalist for the Next Gen Award is a real honour, especially after the recent 30 Under 30 recognition. I see this as a reflection of the hard work that goes on behind the scenes every day at Abu Bakr Supermarkets.
“Our business has always been built around family values, our customers and the communities we serve. I’m fortunate to work alongside a brilliant team, and any success we achieve is down to the people who continue to support and drive the business forward.
“We’re ambitious about the future and want to keep building something that our family, our colleagues and our local communities can be proud of. It’s fantastic to have that journey recognised by the industry.”
Abu Bakr Supermarkets has established a presence across West Yorkshire, serving customers with a broad selection of groceries, fresh produce, halal meat and world foods.
Under Hamza’s leadership, the business continues to focus on customer service, value and developing its offering to meet the needs of changing communities and shopping habits.
Hamza’s ambitions extend beyond the day-to-day running of the business, with a focus on developing the Abu Bakr brand and exploring opportunities to bring its offering to more customers.
The dual recognition from the 30 Under 30 awards and the Asian Trader Awards highlights a significant period for the young managing director and the Batley-based business.
With the Next Gen Award winner set to be announced in London on November 4, Hamza will be hoping to add another accolade to an already promising year.

items.body:
Morrisons Chief AI Officer Mohsen Ghasempour: AI innovation should start with people not tech
Meaningful AI transformation starts with people, not technology. So says Dr Mohsen Ghasempour, Chief AI Officer at Morrisons. Ghasempour recently joined the UK grocery retailer from Kingfisher. He has taken on overall responsibility for data and AI strategy, with a remit spanning customer growth, colleague empowerment, operational efficiency, manufacturing excellence and commercial excellence. He reports directly to Morrisons CEO Rami Baitiéh and took up the role on 1st October.
In a LinkedIn post, Ghasempour said: “Two weeks into my journey at Morrisons, and one of the highlights has been visiting our logistics network and spending time with the brilliant people who keep our operations moving. Behind every product reaching our stores are incredible teams managing enormous complexity, balancing efficiency, availability and the everyday challenges of getting food to customers across the UK.”
He added: “The best AI opportunities come from understanding real problems, and nobody understands those problems better than the people dealing with them every day. That is why I believe meaningful AI transformation starts with people, not technology. A big thank you to Andy Gillies (Logistics Director) and the rest of our fantastic logistics leadership team for sharing their insights, challenges and experiences. Early days, and still a lot to learn, but I am confident we are going to build something special here. Watch this space!”

items.body:
Foot Locker teams with Stylitics as retailer taps AI technology to launch app-based closet builder solution
Foot Locker has developed, in partnership with Stylitics, a new AI powered closet builder, Fits, within its mobile app. In a LinkedIn post, Michael Cera, Interim Head of Product Management and Design at Foot Locker, said: “AI is everywhere. But, at Foot Locker, we challenged ourselves to think about how to improve and make positive change to our customers shopping experience through the use of AI.”
He added: “We engaged with customers, really listened, and in partnership with Stylitics, developed a key new closet builder within the Foot Locker app - let me introduce you to Fits! Start with something you own. Discover personalised outfits built around it. See those looks come to life on a virtual model.”
Customers can upload or take a photo of something they own, discover complete outfits built around it, and visualise those looks on a virtual model. Paired with a cart addition from the model view, the aim is to make purchasing a whole outfit styled around your own products that much easier.
Cera concluded: “This was a collaborative effort across Experience Design, Product Management, E-comm, Brand, and Stylitics, and came to life exactly as we all set out to do. Download or open your Foot Locker app today and give it a try!”

items.body:
Jysk brings unified commerce push to UK and Ireland: this week's biggest retail technology stories
It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Enactor, Ikea, Douyin, Hanshow, Morrisons, Too Good To Go, Duvo, Logile, Frasers Group, M&S, Klarna, and the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
1. Enactor powered unified commerce Jysk roll-out progresses at pace across retailer's UK and Ireland stores
Danish home furnishing retailer Jysk reports that the first of its UK and Ireland stores are now live with its Enactor powered unified commerce platform. In a LinkedIn post, Patrick Gretsch, Retail Operations Expert at Jysk, said: "Two more countries have taken their first steps towards a new way of working, with the first stores in the UK and Ireland now successfully running on our unified commerce platform."
"I had the pleasure of joining the team at our Sallynoggin store in Ireland to experience one of these first transitions firsthand. What stood out was the excellent preparation and collaboration across all departments involved. The result? A smooth and efficient changeover, completed while the store remained open and continued serving customers."
He added: "And this is just the beginning. The roll-out is progressing at pace, with all Jysk stores in both countries expected to be running on the new platform by mid-November. So, what does this mean for our colleagues and customers? For our store teams, unified commerce means simpler processes and new opportunities to serve customers directly on the shop floor. With mobile PoS, colleagues can process payments right where the customer interaction takes place, making the shopping experience more convenient and personal."
"For our customers, it opens the door to additional services. They can, for example, order products in a store and have them delivered directly coming from our warehouse straight to their doorstep. This is what makes unified commerce so exciting: it’s not just about introducing a new platform. It’s about improving the way we work and creating new opportunities to serve our customers."
2. Ikea flagship store brings home furnishing products to Douyin e-commerce shoppers across China
Ingka Group has launched an Ikea Douyin official flagship store in China. The new digital touchpoint will offer more than 6,500 Ikea products across 179 categories, with delivery available in 301 cities across China.
The move brings the retailer in to the short-form video and content commerce platform (a sister platform to TikTok under ByteDance). The store will complement its existing stores, website, app, WeChat and other e-commerce channels in China.
Lydia Song, Ikea China Acting CEO and President and CSO, says: “People in China are increasingly moving between inspiration, discovery and shopping in ways that are highly connected and increasingly digital. Douyin E-commerce gives us an opportunity to meet people in a new context, learn what resonates with them and make Ikea more accessible to more people. This is not simply about adding another sales channel. It is about understanding how we can become part of people’s everyday lives in new and relevant ways.”
Parag Parekh, Chief Digital Officer at Ikea Retail, comments: “Retail is increasingly about being present wherever and whenever people want to meet us, while making those experiences feel like one connected Ikea. What is particularly interesting about new platforms like Douyin E-commerce is the opportunity to learn. They help us understand how inspiration, interaction and commerce are coming closer together, and what that could mean for how we continue to develop the Ikea omnichannel experience.”
3. Kenty Adria and Hanshow tie up brings electronic pricing technology to Konzum and Mercator stores
Hanshow, a Chinese specialist in digital store solutions, has partnered with Kenty Adria, a member of Fortenova Group, to support the large scale roll-out of electronic shelf labels (ESL) across Konzum and Mercator stores in Croatia and Slovenia. Building on pilot projects, the deployment forms part of the broader digital transformation of Fortenova Group's retail network.
At Konzum, electronic pricing has been introduced in more than 200 stores, with a further 260 stores planned for deployment. The largest implementation to date includes 44,000 electronic shelf labels installed at Konzum’s store on Radnička Street in Zagreb. The majority of its retail network, comprising more than 600 stores across Croatia, is expected to be equipped by the end of the 2027 summer season.
At Mercator, electronic shelf labels have so far been installed in 50 stores across Slovenia, with the goal of deploying ESL solutions throughout the entire Mercator retail network by the end of 2027. Across the network, the full roll-out is estimated to require approximately 3.1 million ESLs.
4. Morrisons notches up Too Good To Go surplus food mobile app milestone
Morrisons reports a milestone in its Too Good To Go surplus food partnership. In a LinkedIn post, Rami Baitiéh, CEO at Morrisons, said: “Every second, 80,000 meals go to waste globally. It's a statistic that should make everyone in the food industry pause.”
“When you face numbers of that scale, it is easy to feel that individual action doesn't matter. But at Morrisons, we believe the best way to drive real change is by making it simple, affordable, and rewarding for our customers to make a difference. That is why I'm incredibly proud to share that we have officially saved 4,000,000 meals from going to waste since our partnership with Too Good To Go began in 2019.”
He added: “For those who haven't used it, Too Good To Go is an app that connects people with surplus, unsold food before it gets thrown away. By offering Morrisons Surprise Bags on the app at less than half price, we are ensuring perfectly good, fresh food stays out of the bin while helping households enjoy high quality groceries at a fraction of the cost.”
“Last month, we welcomed Chelsea Kerr from Too Good To Go to our internal event, Teamtalk, and together we celebrated this massive milestone. Behind this achievement is the amazing effort from our colleagues who pack these bags daily, and our customers who step up to rescue them. A huge thank you to everyone involved. To continue this great work, we'll be bringing our new Chilled Surprise Bags, which we're trialing in 25 London stores, to the rest of our supermarkets in the coming months - watch this space!”
5. Kingfisher raids European home improvement retailer OBI to bring in Sebastian Gundel as CEO
Kingfisher, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, has announced the appointment of Sebastian Gundel as Chief Executive Officer, effective 1st February 2027. He will join Kingfisher’s board of directors on the same date.
He brings more than two decades of leadership experience in the home improvement sector, including as Chief Executive Officer at European retailer OBI, where he led the company's evolution from traditional retail to a digitally enabled, customer centric, omnichannel business.
Prior to becoming CEO, he served as Chief Customer & Digital Officer, leading OBI's omnichannel transformation and digital innovation agenda. His responsibilities spanned loyalty, marketplaces and ecosystem development, as well as the expansion of trade propositions.
Claudia Arney, Chair, says: “Following a thorough selection process, the board is delighted to appoint Sebastian as Chief Executive Officer. Sebastian combines deep experience in home improvement retail and clear expertise in Kingfisher’s strategic growth drivers with a strong track record of innovation and operational delivery. He will build on the significant progress made under Thierry Garnier’s leadership while bringing fresh perspectives as we continue to evolve the business. Sebastian has the board’s full support as he leads Kingfisher through its next phase of growth and value creation.”
6. Tomáš Čupr bags $32 million for Duvo, an AI platform born from challenges he encountered while building Rohlik
Duvo, an automation platform that gives teams an AI workforce for their day-to-day operations, has announced a $32 million Series A led by Balderton Capital, with participation from existing investors Index Ventures, Northzone and Credo Ventures. The round brings its total funding to $48 million and will fund its expansion, starting with retailers and CPG companies.
Michael Green is also joining from Databricks as Senior Vice President, Go-to-Market. He previously served as a Senior Vice President at Salesforce. Spencer Insolia recently came onboard as Managing Director, US. He was previously President at Kmart and a Managing Director at Accenture. Christoph Schwaiger, former CEO at Aldi South Holdings, has also signed on as Senior Advisor for Europe.
"For a while I measured AI in heads, counting how many people an agent could replace. It's the wrong unit," says Tomáš Čupr, Co-founder and CEO at Duvo and Founder and Group CEO at Rohlik Group. "At Rohlik, the gains I'd point to came from work nobody had the hours for. Our planners used to check about eight at-risk products a day per market for shortages. Now every signal gets checked, around the clock. We think of it as raising the GDP of every employee: more value from the people a company has, not the same value from fewer of them."
7. First step in a much bigger journey as Frasers Group switches on first D365 WMS warehouse
Frasers Group, whose brands include Sports Direct, House of Fraser, and Flannels, reports that Antrim in Northern Ireland has become the first of its warehouses to go live with a Microsoft Dynamics 365 warehouse management system (WMS).
In a LinkedIn post, Jakob Vestergaard, Product Manager - Warehouse at Frasers Group, said: "Two years of work. One major milestone. We're live. As the first warehouse in the group to adopt D365 WMS, Antrim marks an important milestone in our wider warehouse transformation journey."
"Over the last few years, Frasers Group has invested heavily in elevating our stores. This programme is about taking the next step by elevating the warehouse operations that power them, creating a more scalable, visible and consistent platform to support our stores, brands and customers. This achievement would not have been possible without the dedication of teams across the business and our partners."
He concluded: "Go live is a major achievement, but it isn't the end of the story. Over the coming months we'll continue working with our warehouse teams, Microsoft, Binary and InterRadish to refine the solution, introduce additional capabilities and build out the global warehouse template that will support future warehouse deployments across Frasers Group. This is the first step in a much bigger journey. Looking forward to what comes next."
8. Morrisons taps Logile to enhance store planning across supermarket, convenience, logistics sites
Morrisons has selected Logile as it looks to enhance store workload planning across the UK grocery retailer’s business. The agreement covers its supermarket and convenience store estate alongside its logistics network.
Morrisons is implementing Logile software in a bid to simplify central planning, replacing time-consuming manual spreadsheets with optimised operational data and intelligence. By delivering clearer visibility into store workload requirements, it says that central operations can provide accurate, reliable insight across the estate, allowing teams to focus on better supporting store operations.
“Getting colleagues where customers need them most is the heart of what we do, and at our scale you need a reliable, shared foundation to get that right,” says Alex Rose, Head of Productivity at Morrisons. “A large supermarket and a local convenience store operate differently so our planning has to flex to those local needs while keeping central support consistent. When our store managers have plans they can depend on, they spend less time managing admin and more time supporting their colleagues and serving customers.”
9. 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards UK Retailer of the Year finalists include Waitrose, Toolstation, and Morrisons
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Most Innovative UK Retailer category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
10. Klarna goes live on M&S.com to bring BNPL service to fashion, home and beauty customers
Klarna reports that it is now available as a payment option at Marks & Spencer for fashion, home and beauty purchases online. Shoppers on M&S.com and the UK retailer’s app can now tap Klarna and split the cost into three equal, interest free payments with, according to a press release, transparent terms and no revolving balance.
"People deserve flexibility without paying interest for it, so our goal is simple: meet them wherever they shop," says Klarna Head of UK, Ireland & Western & Southern Europe, Raji Behal. "M&S is a beloved British icon that brings second to none quality and value to millions of shoppers every day. We’re proud to now offer them a transparent way to spread the cost with no interest and a clear end date."
Katherine Carlson, Director of Financial Services at M&S, says: “We are always looking for ways to make it easier for our customers to shop with us. Customers shopping on M&S.com and through our app can now spread the cost in three interest free payments with Klarna, offering more flexibility in how they pay for the things they love.”

2026 RTIH Innovation Awards UK Technology Vendor finalists include Focal Systems, Datitude, GoPlaces
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards UK Technology Vendor of the Year category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Technology Vendor of the Year (UK) finalists as follows:
Attensi
Attensi helps retailers train frontline colleagues through practice, not paperwork. Its platform combines behavioural psychology, game design and AI.
Colleagues rehearse real customer conversations with lifelike AI characters in RealTalk, play gamified store simulations and get instant feedback until they feel confident. Embla, Attensi's AI co-designer, lets retail L&D teams build and update training in minutes, while Insights shows exactly which skills are improving.
In the past year, B&Q used RealTalk to strengthen selling and coaching for around 2,500 showroom colleagues and managers, and IHOP replaced paper-based training across more than 1,700 restaurants. Circle K has engaged 14,000 store staff across eight countries.
Datitude
Every new retail system solves a problem. Each also adds another version of the truth. Datitude fixes that. Its unified data platform brings data from retailers' systems into one trusted foundation, so every team, BI tool and AI model works from the same numbers.
In 2026 it added a Semantic Layer, giving everyone shared business definitions, and an AI Gateway, letting retailers use their choice of AI on governed data. A fully managed platform and service, run by a team who get retail, tech and data. Most clients work with Datitude for years. Many new ones come through recommendation.
Focal Systems
Focal Systems uses fixed cameras and computer vision to keep supermarket shelves full. Its cameras photograph every shelf every hour, spot gaps, and help staff fix them. At Morrisons, Focal covers around 500 supermarkets.
The time to spot an empty shelf fell from 12 to 24 hours to about 30 minutes, on-shelf availability rose 2 to 4%, and Morrisons saved more than £10 million a year in labour. In the past year, Focal and Morrisons went further: trialling cameras in the back room, and rebuilding the metrics so every store's numbers are checked against a measured standard.
GoPlaces
Go Places is a creative company with a heart of analytics: part agency, part software developer, built for enterprise brands on TikTok Shop. It built OnePlace, the first unified analytics and decision-intelligence platform for the channel, because the data problem underneath it was nobody else's priority.
In two years, it has gone from two founders to a team of 50+, 22 major brands including TRIP, PerfectTed, The Body Shop, Haleon and Sensodyne, £3 milion ARR and the UK's largest live shopping operation by studio count. Brands on OnePlace average a 25% ROI improvement.
Quail Digital
Quail Digital's Pro12 retail headset system is redefining how modern retailers communicate and operate. More than a wireless headset, Pro12 combines crystal clear team communication with built-in speech recognition, AI integration, intelligent safety alerts and an open platform that connects colleagues, technology and store operations.
Designed for today's connected retail environment, it empowers store teams to work more efficiently, make faster decisions and remain focused on serving customers. By improving store efficiency and employee wellbeing, the Pro12 retail headset system helps retailers deliver a safer, more productive workplace and an exceptional customer experience, while laying the foundation for Quail Digital's vision of the intelligent connected store.
Quin AI
Quin AI gives retailers a real-time customer intelligence layer. Its three AI agents build a live customer context for every shopper, optimise offers and recommend complementary products, and feed that context into enterprise systems, including LLMs.
At Koçtaş A.Ş., Kingfisher's home improvement retailer in Türkiye, Quin lifted conversion 1.63x and has sustained 10–15% incremental revenue since 2024, with campaign cost below 3%. The same context guides Koçtaş's LLM-powered chatbot, routing conversations to live agents with 90% accuracy; around 40% of routed calls convert to a sale.
Webtrends Optimize
Halfords had begun embarking on a personalisation journey prior to working with Webtrends Optimize but the latter's role as conversion rate optimisation expert was to scale personalisation across the retailer's website and improve users' experiences by streamlining processes and enhancing its personalisation programme to provide the best experience for visitors.
Xiatech
Retailers want AI but lack the foundation. Systems are not connected, data is not unified and processes are manual. Xfuze, an agentic orchestration platform, is that agentic ready foundation. It unifies integration and orchestration, data management, insights and analytics, and agentic AI in one platform. The CHIP family of AI agents, led by CHIP Assist, an AI assistant, gives teams answers.
Line of business Xfuze Agents, governed in the Xfuze AI Control Tower, replenish stock, answer shoppers and much more. Moss, Reiss, WHSmith and Flying Tiger Copenhagen use Xfuze.

2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Global Technology Vendor finalists include Deliverect, Solink, Sitoo
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Global Technology Vendor of the Year category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Technology Vendor of the Year (Rest of World) finalists as follows:
Deliverect
Deliverect has partnered with Asda Express to simplify on-demand retail operations across its estate, consolidating separate Uber Eats, Deliveroo and Just Eat picking workflows into one unified application.
Rolled out across the Asda Express estate, the technology gives store teams a single process for managing and picking marketplace orders, reducing operational complexity while significantly improving product availability and picking accuracy. The simpler experience has also driven improved staff NPS.
Beyond operational efficiency, the initiative provides the technology infrastructure underpinning Asda Express's c-commerce success, creating a scalable ecosystem where additional digital channels and capabilities can be introduced easily as and when required.
Fynd
Fynd is a unified commerce platform. Between September 2025 and September 2026, it partnered with retailers across Malaysia, Indonesia, Qatar, India and the UAE to transform both customer experience and back-end operations on one platform spanning PoS, order management, marketplaces, logistics, AI data automation and AI content.
Its flagship build for QSR Brands saw daily orders growing a sustained 7.0% over the pre-Fynd baseline for Hugo Boss (UAE), REDTAG, Qatar’s beauty houses and Indian brands delivered outcomes such as 259k+ inventory updates synced and 48% marketplace revenue growth.
HelmCore
HelmCore is a retail operational intelligence platform built for distributed retail estates. It correlates PoS, network, IoT and energy signals from every site, collapses related events into single incidents, then applies AI to surface root cause and translate each incident into real-time financial impact using customer validated cost parameters.
Every customer runs on an isolated, single-tenant instance, with a sanitisation layer stripping sensitive data before it reaches the cloud model. Built and headquartered in Sligo, Ireland, HelmCore works with multi-site retailers across convenience and fuel, and grocery and general retail.
Lily AI
Before a product reaches a consumer, an AI system increasingly decides whether it gets discovered or recommended. Lily AI has spent six years making products understandable to these systems. Launched in August 2026, Lily Max turns that intelligence into action: agents identify missing product information, enrich it in consumer language, test changes against controls and deploy what works across paid media and AI discovery.
Used by retailers and brands including Marks & Spencer, Vuori, Hibbett Sports, Shiseido and Coach, Lily has run 1,000+ controlled tests. Lily Max makes products understandable to AI, and proves the commercial impact when they are.
Mys Tyler
Fashion-tech startup, Mys Tyler partnered with City Chic to improve shopper fit confidence and reduce online returns. Using Mys Tyler’s FitCheck technology, the partnership combined diverse creators, visual fit reviews and structured fit data.
This content was embedded on City Chic’s product pages across Australia, New Zealand and the US. Across 120 products and 5,831 units sold, City Chic recorded 7% fewer returns in Australia and New Zealand, and 10% fewer returns in the US, with reductions of up to 62% on some garments, reducing reverse logistics costs and wasted stock, and showing what a retailer-technology partnership can deliver.
Revieve
Revieve is advancing the next era of beauty commerce through purpose built industry intelligence. At the centre of its approach is BeautyCatalyst, Revieve's Beauty Commerce Intelligence Platform, connecting beauty expertise, consumer understanding and commerce to help brands and retailers create more relevant consumer experiences and make more informed decisions across their businesses.
ShopperAI
ShopperAI is an AI powered retail floor intelligence platform that turns existing store CCTV cameras into real-time operational insights without requiring hardware installation.
By continuously analysing the sales floor using computer vision with over 95% accuracy, ShopperAI instantly detects stockout events, planogram deviations, blocked aisles, and shrink exposure. The system routes real-time priorities directly to store staff and managers via existing communication channels, protecting revenue and boosting margins. Operating at scale across hundreds of stores, ShopperAI bridges the gap between digital intelligence and physical retail execution seamlessly.
Solink
Solink has created the Solink Vision Intelligence Platform, an outcome driven operational layer that converts legacy, passive video infrastructure into an active, intelligent framework. It is hardware agnostic, bridging the gap between siloed video environments and enterprise data by natively integrating with more than 375 applications, access control mechanisms, and IoT systems.
Sitoo
Retail stores are being asked to do more: sell, fulfil and manage returns across stores and online sales channels while delivering increasingly personalised customer experiences.
Sitoo makes unified commerce work in the store. Its cloud native Unified Commerce Platform, anchored by PoS, connects stores and online sales channels in real-time, turning inventory, customer, order and cross-channel information into action.
Trusted by 300+ retailers and compliant in 40+ markets, Sitoo helps retailers increase sales, improve inventory confidence, enable cross-channel selling, fulfilment and returns, and empower associates to deliver better customer experiences.
Talkdesk
Talkdesk provides contact centre and customer experience automation solutions purpose-built for modern retail. The platform unifies the shopper journey, putting people and AI to work where each makes the biggest difference.
AI agents resolve transaction heavy tasks like processing order status, managing returns, and proactively re-engaging abandoned shopping carts. Contact centre agents and in-store associates have access to AI guidance and a shared view of the customer, helping them deliver personalised service in every interaction.
Retailers gain a continuous view of the customer across digital, contact centre, and in-person touchpoints, turning disconnected interactions into connected experiences that build lasting loyalty.

Our 2026 Inclusive Technology Innovation finalists as follows:
Hockerty
Nearly a third of Hockerty's new customers have a BMI over 30, going by the height and weight they enter at checkout. In Germany, France, Italy and Spain that share is 1.6 to 2.2 times the rate among men in the general population.
Made to measure has no size chart to fall off, and larger bodies have noticed. Hockerty's September 2026 analysis puts numbers on it, and it has built on that: a body profile from three numbers, a try-on on the customer's own photo, and pages written for bigger and taller men.
Nūl
Nūl is an agentic AI platform helping fashion and retail teams make better inventory decisions before costly mistakes become excess stock, markdowns or missed sales.
It has worked with a retailer in Singapore and South East Asia called Our Barehands, which creates sustainable livelihoods for artisanal communities, working with displaced or refugee communities, and combines made-to-order and off-the-rack fashion for a more sustainable business model. Yet fragmented systems, manual processes and limited visibility across materials, production, inventory and customer orders made this model difficult to scale.
Nūl adapted its existing platform to cover end to end agentic forecasting and production, ensuring an AI powered integrated fashion supply chain. The project demonstrates how human centred AI can reduce complexity and support scalable, purpose led growth for mission driven brands.
Sticky
Sticky used its no-code platform to make stadium hospitality more accessible for both guests and operational teams.
Following a deployment at Manchester United, it created accessible ordering across four dedicated stadium areas, using large format QR codes so wheelchair users and other guests could order without leaving their seats. The same drag and drop platform enabled colour blind safe kitchen display screens, autism friendly text and simplified controls, reducing cognitive load throughout the ordering journey.
Behind the scenes, Bluetooth enabled asset geotagging and an offline Traffic Light Status dashboard improved wayfinding for operational staff, demonstrating how accessibility can be designed into the holistic venue experience.
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.body:
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Startup of the Year finalists include Augmodo and Theseus Robotics
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Startup of the Year category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Startup of the Year finalists as follows:
Augmodo
Augmodo builds physical AI infrastructure powered by wearable computer vision for frontline retail teams. A frontline worker wears a passive Smartbadge during standard shifts, automatically building a live 3D map of shelf inventory to spot out-of-stocks, gaps, and misplaced items in real-time with zero manual scanning or operational change.
Founded in 2023 by Ross Finman, who sold his last start up to Niantic and led the mapping team behind Pokémon GO, Augmodo expanded from 8 to 165 stores in under a year, raising nearly $60 million at a $350 million valuation. Chemist Warehouse achieved 30%+ shelf gap reductions.
Clavis Studio
AI visual commerce tool that uses furniture retailers' product catalog to design their shoppers' rooms such that shoppers can 'shop the look' according to their design preference and budget.
Clavis AI provides a whitelabelled, fully embedded AI design tool for furniture retailers to offer personalised interior design to their shoppers online and instore. Fully immersive with deep data analytics providing unrivalled insight into consumer behaviour.
Lyzer
Lyzer is a Lisbon-based logistics-as-a-service (LaaS) startup, launched in September 2024 by the founders of 360hyper and SPEAK. Its platform brings orders from stores, online shops and marketplaces into one system and runs smart task allocation, guided picking and route optimisation, so retailers can turn existing stores into fulfilment hubs.
In two years, Lyzer has processed over 1.1 million orders worth more than €330 million in GMV, enabled Staples Portugal to offer same-day delivery within four hours, opened a Spanish subsidiary and raised over €10 million from Indico Capital Partners, Lince Capital, LC Ventures and C2 Capital.
Minimist
Minimist is the recommerce operating system for charity retail. Every donated item is a one-off with no barcode, no SKU and no product data, so listing one by hand takes up to 10 minutes and 97% of donated stock never goes online at all.
Minimist turns one photo into a priced, described, live listing across eight marketplaces in 30 seconds. In our first year in market we have signed 28 charity retailers across the UK, Ireland and Australia, including Salvation Army, Vision Ireland and Helen and Douglas House. Together they have listed 73,844 donated items and sold 31,580 of them, raising 1,409,994 euros for their causes.
M11 Labs
M11 Labs is an agentic commerce lab helping good products win in a zero-trust internet. The M11 platform puts specialised AI agents to work on a brand's online store across four areas: fact checking every claim against independent evidence, correcting what AI assistants say, completing the product data machines need, and tracking competitor threats.
Everything rolls into one Commercial Score and a prioritised fix list, which M11 agents draft and the brand approves. Within months of launch M11 agents have scanned 1,500+ brands, stress tested 6,500+ claims, published a state of the category scan of the skincare industry, and launched OpenMarket, the first multi-agent marketplace.
Neato
Neato is a second party (2P) e-commerce model that gives consumer brands one accountable partner to grow across fragmented online channels. Neato purchases inventory directly, becomes the seller of record, and manages marketplace execution across pricing, listings, creative, advertising, logistics, reporting, and brand protection.
Over the past year, the company extended this model beyond Amazon into TikTok Shop, direct-to-consumer, social commerce, and Walmart, supported by a new Las Vegas operations hub, and AI enabled workflows. By bringing people, inventory, technology, and execution together, Neato aims to make marketplace growth more coordinated, measurable, and profitable for brands and shoppers.
SquareBySquare
SquareBySquare turns an online purchase into real, mapped rainforest protection. Customers choose a square metre of rainforest, name it, receive a personalised certificate and see it on a live public map.
StudioGo
StudioGo is a workflow platform designed to eliminate content bottlenecks and provide complete visibility across the product imagery lifecycle.
By connecting planning, production, approval, asset management, and publication into a single workflow, StudioGO helps retail, e-commerce, creative, marketing, and studio teams move products from sample arrival to customer facing channels faster and with greater consistency.
TerzyApp
TerzyApp turns two ordinary phone photos into 32 body measurements, letting people order made-to-measure clothing online and matching them with verified independent tailors.
Payments and payouts run across 37 countries and the tailor is paid only after successful delivery. It combines live AI body measurement, a verified tailor marketplace and cross-border money rails in one shipped product - made-to-measure clothing from your phone. TerzyApp UK is pre-revenue, with a working iOS app in TestFlight beta and an AI measurement engine running in production on cloud GPU, ahead of a UK launch.
Theseus Robotics
Theseus Robotics (Zürich; Y Combinator backed) has buillt Domi, a wheeled, two-armed robot that restocks supermarket shelves overnight.
Domi tows a trolley of stock to the aisle and places products on the shelf. An AI model trained on Theseus's own demonstrations moves the arms; when Domi meets something new, an operator can step in remotely and the correction becomes training data.
No store retrofit, no capex: a monthly fee per robot. Founded by a team from ETH Zürich, Carnegie Mellon and Flink Robotics, Theseus had Domi restocking autonomously within five weeks of the robot's delivery and is preparing retailer pilots for 2027.

items.body:
UK home improvement retailer B&Q expands its fast delivery options with Deliveroo and Gophr tie up
B&Q is ramping up its fast delivery push with the launch of TradePoint Express, a same-day delivery service exclusively for trade customers, in partnership with Gophr. The retailer has also expanded its Deliveroo partnership to more than 100 stores nationwide following a trial. Customers can now access up to more than 9,000 home improvement products through Deliveroo, with orders delivered in as little as 35 minutes.
The partnership with Gophr will allow Business Development Managers to arrange deliveries, either within two hours or for a pre-booked two-hour slot same-day, for TradePoint members from B&Q's standalone TradePoint store in Barking and 123 participating B&Q stores across the UK. The service is set to expand to all TradePoint stores later this year.
The launch builds on the introduction of Marketplace Click & Collect. Customers can now choose from an expanding range of collection and delivery options designed to suit planned projects, urgent repairs and last minute requirements.
Amélie Gallichan Todd, Supply & Logistics Director at B&Q, says: “We're continually evolving the ways customers can shop with B&Q, making it faster and more convenient to access the products they need. The launch of TradePoint Express to more than 100 stores is an important step in that journey, giving both trade and retail customers greater flexibility through a range of delivery options designed to suit different project needs. As our customer expectations continue to evolve, we’re focused on making it easier for them to get the right products, exactly when and where they need them.”
John Morgan, Director of TradePoint, says: "Time is one of the most valuable resources for trade professionals. TradePoint Express has been designed to help our members spend less time collecting materials and more time focused on the job. By working with our TradePoint Business Development Managers and Gophr, we're providing a flexible same-day delivery service that helps keep projects moving and supports customers when timing matters most."
Graham Smith, Commercial Director at Gophr, says: “Gophr’s partnership with B&Q supporting the launch of TradePoint Express will help deliver a faster, more convenient service for trade customers. Our technology and delivery network enable flexible, same-day fulfilment that meets the needs of busy professionals, helping products move quickly and efficiently from store to site.”
Suzy McClintock, VP of Consumer at Deliveroo, comments: “Deliveroo customers frequently use the platform for their home improvement needs, as they seek out quick and convenient delivery during those DIY emergencies. By expanding our successful partnership with B&Q nationwide, more customers than ever can keep those home improvement projects moving, with access to what they need, when they need it. Whether it’s paint or power tools, we can have them delivered to your doorstep in as little as 25 minutes.”
Suzy McClintock, VP of Consumer at Deliveroo, adds: “Deliveroo customers frequently use the platform for their home improvement needs, as they seek out quick and convenient delivery during those DIY emergencies. items.title: 'TV and cheap booze' blamed for landlord quitting
items.summary: Lincolnshire has lost 27% of its pubs and bars since 2009 and some are calling on the government to act against cheap supermarket booze.
items.body:
'TV and cheap booze' blamed for landlord quitting
- Published
Former pub landlord Patrick Hughes is blunt when explaining why he has called time on his tenure behind the bar.
"I thought there was a gap in the market but there was no market for the gap", he said.
The 66-year-old took over The Royal Mail Cart pub in Spalding, in August 2025, hoping to attract customers with live music nights and "a sense of community".
Just over a year on he is packing boxes and looking around the empty rooms after he quit his tenancy with the pub's owner, Stonegate Group.
The government said it was supporting pubs with business rates discounts.
Patrick told BBC Politics North that he blames a perfect storm of rising utility and wage prices, people's changing habits and major roadworks directly outside the pub, which began in the summer.
"These days people are used to staying at home, watching TV, having cheap drink from the supermarket or off licence and getting food deliveries," he said.
"To make a pub like this work you need to turn over Â£12,000 a week, some weeks we were doing quite well, around Â£8,000, but once the road works began outside that went down quite dramatically."
Figures from the Office for National Statistics, external show that 27% of pubs and bars in Lincolnshire closed between 2009 and 2025. That is a drop from 710 to 515.
In South Holland, of which Spalding is a part, the rate is almost double that, at 53%, a drop from 75 to 35. That is also way above the England average of 19%.
"The government needs to look at the low cost of alcohol in supermarkets primarily," said Patrick.
"Certainly the taxation in supermarkets needs to be looked at to bring about some kind of equilibrium."
Duty paid on draught alcohol in pubs and bars is up to 11 pence cheaper than that sold in supermarkets.
But other costs associated with running a business still makes supermarket alcohol cheaper overall.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced a 20% cut in business rates for qualifying pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England, effective from April 2027.
Emma McClarkin OBE, chief executive of the British Beer and Pub Association, says they want that to be made permanent at the Budget this month, "alongside a freeze in beer duty and a widening of the draft discount".
"We're set to lose one pub a day by the end of the year and 295 have closed already," she said.
"When a pub does close, it's not just the front door that's closing, it's the heritage, the culture, the economic contribution to society and the social value."
Just outside Spalding, The Ship Inn pub stands by the River Welland in the small hamlet of Surfleet Seas End.
"There used to be tables and chairs with people eating food and drinking by the river," said Mark Newlands, who lives a few doors down.
The pub closed last year but now some locals, led by Mark, have formed The Shipmates group to try to raise Â£600,000 to buy and run it.
So far they have managed to get the pub listed as An Asset of Community Value under the Localism Act 2011. That gives them the right to bid for the property, if it goes up for sale.
"People have become fed up of the Covid way of living and they want to see their pub open," said Mark.
"The indications from smaller and larger investors is that it's worth doing and we've proven to our own satisfaction that it is a viable business."
An HM Treasury spokesperson said: "The Chancellor prioritised support for the hospitality industry in his first week in the job when he cut business rates by 20% for pubs, social clubs and live music venues - saving thousands of locals over Â£1,000 a year."
Stonegate has been approached by the BBC for comment.

items.body:
Footasylum’s AutoStore delivers goods as THG Fulfil wraps first external build ahead of peak season
THG Fulfil recently completed its first AutoStore implementation for an external retailer. Footasylum’s automated fulfilment operation is now live and delivering 212% of the output of the retailer’s previous operation, from fewer than half the picking stations.
Announced in June, the system processed its first customer order on 28th August and went fully live on 14th September. According to those involved, the build was delivered two months faster than the original project plan, with less than six months between contract signature and first order. A fleet of 85 AutoStore R5 robots operates across 96,000 bin locations, with 100% of Footasylum’s live SKU range stored in the grid and system uptime holding at 99.8%.
Before construction began, the two teams ran 80,000 simulations using Footasylum’s order history, seasonal demand curves and product data to determine the optimum number of robots and ports. At the heart of the live operation is THG Fulfil’s proprietary Warehouse Control System (WCS), developed over five years inside its own AutoStore network. Its in-house development team is refining the WCS after go-live, using live order data to improve bin sequencing, batching and stock positioning.
The project was delivered under a hybrid commercial model combining elements of capital investment and THG Fulfil’s robotics-as-a-service (RaaS) offering, structured specifically around Footasylum’s requirements.

items.body:
AI doubts, digital threats, and surplus food milestones: the retail technology week in numbers
Do you like numbers? Do you like retail technology news? Then this is the article for you. Including Duvo, TFG London, Bain & Company, M&S, Morrisons, Lidl GB, Omnisend, Marklo, Ikea, Miracly, Pricer, Orange, and Frasers Group.
561...Pricer has been selected by Orange, a telecommunications operator in France, to digitalise its retail store network. The project encompasses 561 stores with an average size of 120 m² over the next two years.
The agreement covers the complete deployment of Pricer’s electronic shelf label (ESL) solution, including hardware, infrastructure, attachment solutions, installation, and cloud management via the Plaza platform under a long-term maintenance contract. It includes annual recurring SaaS and maintenance revenue. Orange chose Pricer following pilot programmes across multiple store locations.
28% of UK consumers do not trust artificial intelligence in retail at all, as retailers such as Morrisons introduce new technology to the weekly shop, according to research from e-commerce marketing platform Omnisend.
The company surveyed 1,086 Brits for this. 29% are concerned that AI will lead to job losses on the high street. 27% feel their activity is being tracked by supermarkets, while 53% believe loyalty schemes such as Tesco Clubcard and Sainsbury's Nectar monitor their spending habits.
The findings come as Morrisons trials Instacart's AI powered Caper smart trolleys at a Preston store, becoming the first UK retailer to introduce the technology. Elsewhere, Lidl extended its Lidl & Go trial to another 37 stores during July, allowing customers to scan products through the Lidl Plus app and track their spending and savings in real-time
55% of respondents have used a scan-as-you-shop device in a supermarket. Among those who have tried the technology, 70% used it to save time at the checkout, while 24% tapped it to help stick to a budget. A further 5% wanted to reduce the amount of interaction they had with supermarket staff. Just 8% of all respondents said scan-as-you-shop devices make them feel as though their every move is being tracked, while 20% said the technology makes their weekly shop more efficient.
$5 million...Marklo has announced $5 million in seed funding led by Forerunner, with participation from Freestyle Capital. It has also opened its public beta. Marklo is an agentic marketing platform for brands running on Shopify that, according to those involved, understands what is happening across the business, identifies the next revenue opportunity and proactively builds the work for marketers to review and approve.
Used by DTC brands including Away, Clare V., Monica + Andy, Maya Brenner and Latico Leathers, Marklo is pitched as knowing what a brand has sold, what it has marketed, what's in stock and what's coming next, and what's happening outside the brand: what competitors are promoting, what's trending on social and where the category is moving. It reads all of it to determine which campaigns to run next, then builds the work itself: the calendar, the content, the approvals and the team handoffs that used to happen by hand.
"Every tool in a brand's stack is getting AI, but each one only sees its own corner of the business," says Jessica Herrin, Founder and CEO at Marklo (who previously founded Stella & Dot Brands). "Great merchants don't work that way. You can't decide what to market next without knowing what sold, what's in stock, what you've already promoted, what's coming, and what the rest of your category is doing. Marklo sees all of it, spots the next opportunity and gets the work moving."
$32 million...Duvo, an automation platform that gives teams an AI workforce for their day-to-day operations, has announced a $32 million Series A led by Balderton Capital, with participation from existing investors Index Ventures, Northzone and Credo Ventures. The round brings its total funding to $48 million and will fund its expansion, starting with retailers and CPG companies.
Michael Green is also joining from Databricks as Senior Vice President, Go-to-Market. He previously served as a Senior Vice President at Salesforce. Spencer Insolia recently came onboard as Managing Director, US. He was previously President at Kmart and a Managing Director at Accenture. Christoph Schwaiger, former CEO at Aldi South Holdings, has also signed on as Senior Advisor for Europe.
"For a while I measured AI in heads, counting how many people an agent could replace. It's the wrong unit," says Tomáš Čupr, Co-founder and CEO at Duvo and Founder and Group CEO at Rohlik Group. "At Rohlik, the gains I'd point to came from work nobody had the hours for. Our planners used to check about eight at-risk products a day per market for shortages. Now every signal gets checked, around the clock. We think of it as raising the GDP of every employee: more value from the people a company has, not the same value from fewer of them."
$2 million...Miracly, a GEO and AI operating system for marketing teams and agencies developed by The Wild Ventures, the company behind Scandinavian home decor brand Wild Palace, has announced a $2 million pre-seed round led by Beenext Ventures and Lotus alongside a Swedish family office, with existing investors including Stefan Lindeberg, Founder at VC firm Creandum; Alex Bouaziz, Founder and CEO at Deel; Thomas Ekman, Founder at 6GAI and former CEO at Axel Johnson publ, Dustin and Tele2; Hedda Baverud Olsson, Founder and CEO at Lassie, and Parham Benisi, Partner at Pophouse.
The company publicly launches this week. Pre-launch it has landed customers including Dreams, Acclime, Pixi Beauty, Andy Okay and Duellix.
“We’re seeing an incredible demand for Miracly’s AI marketing platform. Companies all over the world are impacted by decreasing organic traffic from Google and increasing cost of performance marketing,” says Bjorn Bergstrom, Co-founder at Miracly.
“We started out with GEO analytics and AI content generation, but are rapidly becoming a holistic AI marketing platform based on the demand and opportunity we’re seeing in the market. Marketing and agency teams are becoming hybrid marketing and tech organisations and need to develop incredibly quickly to keep up with the changes. Miracly is here to guide them through this shift into an AI first era with completely customised recommendations and agentic flows.”
$248.9 billion and $10.8 trillion...The owner of fashion brands Hobbs, Whistles and Phase Eight, TFG London, was this week hit by a cyber attack affecting some of its IT systems. The company identified the incident on Sunday 11th October and said it was investigating with the help of external cyber security specialists. Stores remained open, but some website functions were unavailable while the investigation continued.
TFG said there was no reason to believe payment information was at risk, although the investigation into the extent of the breach is ongoing. The incident came a week after Asos disclosed that an unauthorised party had accessed some personal data, including customers’ names and contact details. H&M is also investigating claims it was targeted by cyber criminals.
Susannah Streeter, Chief Investment Strategist, Wealth Club, says: “Corporate defences are looking dangerously thin amid an onslaught of cyber attacks against businesses. This spate of infiltrations into retailers’ systems should serve as a brutal alarm call for organisations grappling with increasingly sophisticated digital threats. Big names are littering the landscape, with Marks & Spencer badly affected last year, Asos still reeling from its breach and now household names Hobbs, Whistles and Phase Eight brought into the cyber attack wave with the attack on TFG London’s IT systems."
"It comes hot on the heels of an audacious attack on supermarket refrigeration systems in France, which saw hackers remotely manipulate cooling controls, sending temperatures soaring and leaving hundreds of stores facing spoiled food, fires and potentially millions of euros in losses. The scale of the threat is staggering, with Gartner forecasting that global spending on information security will reach $248.9 billion this year, while Cybersecurity Ventures has estimated that cybercrime costs have expanded to $10.8 trillion annually.”
She adds: "That gulf underlines the enormous financial damage cyber attacks can inflict and raises questions about vulnerabilities in systems. The amount being spent on protection is surging, with forecasts that there will be a much bigger shift away from reactive detection and response strategies towards pre-emptive solutions, reliant on advanced AI tools. It demonstrates the considerable opportunities ahead for firms at the forefront of cyber defence. It is clear that pressure is mounting on businesses to strengthen their defences as attacks become increasingly sophisticated."
"Cyber security can no longer be treated as a back office IT issue or a cost to be trimmed when budgets come under pressure. Organisations need to be shoring up their defences before attackers find a way in, rather than scrambling to contain the damage afterwards. Retailers are particularly attractive targets, sitting on valuable customer data and relying on interconnected systems to keep everything from online orders to supply chains moving. The consequences of a breach can stretch far beyond stolen information, hitting sales, disrupting operations and eroding customer trust."
15...UNiDAYS, a verification platform for students, is partnering with M&S. The tie gives its student community in the UK access to 15% off M&S’s clothing, home, and beauty ranges. This is available for purchases made online.
Richard Stoker, Affiliate Partnerships Manager at M&S, says: “Partnering with UNiDAYS is a brilliant way for us to introduce more students and recent graduates to M&S and help them discover the style, quality and value we offer across clothing, home and beauty. With an exclusive 15% discount, they can make their money go further as they prepare for university, settle into student life or take their first steps into the world of work.”
Alex Gallagher, Chief Strategy Officer at UNiDAYS, says: “We’re delighted to partner with M&S and help open up one of Britain’s most iconic heritage retailers to students and graduates across the UK. For more than 140 years, M&S has been known for its quality, style, and exceptional value, and we’re excited to make its fashion offering more accessible to the next generation of shoppers.”
4,000,000...Morrisons reports a milestone in its Too Good To Go surplus food partnership. In a LinkedIn post, Rami Baitiéh, CEO at Morrisons, said: “Every second, 80,000 meals go to waste globally. It's a statistic that should make everyone in the food industry pause.”
“When you face numbers of that scale, it is easy to feel that individual action doesn't matter. But at Morrisons, we believe the best way to drive real change is by making it simple, affordable, and rewarding for our customers to make a difference. That is why I'm incredibly proud to share that we have officially saved 4,000,000 meals from going to waste since our partnership with Too Good To Go began in 2019.”
He added: “For those who haven't used it, Too Good To Go is an app that connects people with surplus, unsold food before it gets thrown away. By offering Morrisons Surprise Bags on the app at less than half price, we are ensuring perfectly good, fresh food stays out of the bin while helping households enjoy high quality groceries at a fraction of the cost.”
“Last month, we welcomed Chelsea Kerr from Too Good To Go to our internal event, Teamtalk, and together we celebrated this massive milestone. Behind this achievement is the amazing effort from our colleagues who pack these bags daily, and our customers who step up to rescue them. A huge thank you to everyone involved. To continue this great work, we'll be bringing our new Chilled Surprise Bags, which we're trialing in 25 London stores, to the rest of our supermarkets in the coming months - watch this space!”
6,500 and 179...Ingka Group has launched an Ikea Douyin official flagship store in China. The new digital touchpoint will offer more than 6,500 Ikea products across 179 categories, with delivery available in 301 cities across China.
The move brings the retailer in to the short-form video and content commerce platform (a sister platform to TikTok under ByteDance). The store will complement its existing stores, website, app, WeChat and other e-commerce channels in China.
Lydia Song, Ikea China Acting CEO and President and CSO, says: “People in China are increasingly moving between inspiration, discovery and shopping in ways that are highly connected and increasingly digital. Douyin E-commerce gives us an opportunity to meet people in a new context, learn what resonates with them and make Ikea more accessible to more people. This is not simply about adding another sales channel. It is about understanding how we can become part of people’s everyday lives in new and relevant ways.”
Parag Parekh, Chief Digital Officer at Ikea Retail, comments: “Retail is increasingly about being present wherever and whenever people want to meet us, while making those experiences feel like one connected Ikea. What is particularly interesting about new platforms like Douyin E-commerce is the opportunity to learn. They help us understand how inspiration, interaction and commerce are coming closer together, and what that could mean for how we continue to develop the Ikea omnichannel experience.”
$85 billion...US retail sales over the Black Friday through Cyber Monday weekend are expected to top $85 billion, accounting for 8.5% of 2026 holiday sales, according to Bain & Company research. Sales growth during the weekend is set to rise 8.75% year over year, outpacing Bain's total holiday season growth forecast of 4.5%.
Using proprietary credit card data from Pyxis, Bain's consumer intelligence division, its report finds that Black Friday is likely to remain the leading sales day of the holiday season as consumers continue to treat it as the official kick-off. In fact, 64% of consumers surveyed will be out in force on Black Friday, up from 55% in 2025. Cyber Monday has also continued to gain popularity and is expected to crack the top five sales days this year, as more shoppers say they will do their holiday shopping online. 44% of consumers surveyed plan to shop Cyber Monday, compared to 41% last year.
Bains’s survey of US consumers finds that 70% plan to shop Black Friday and/or Cyber Monday, up from 64% last year, and more than 90% are looking to do so on either those days or another major sales event. The final two weekends before Christmas carry just as much weight, however. In 2025, six of the top ten sales days landed in that window. Overall, Bain forecasts US holiday sales will top $1 trillion for the first time, driven by in-store sales and rising e-commerce.
"Black Friday and Cyber Monday are becoming increasingly important battlegrounds for retailers, especially as US consumers prioritise value and deal heavy shopping days," says Aaron Cheris, Global Head of Retail at Bain & Company. "Retailers that capitalise on these crucial sales days with personalised promotions, can’t miss events, and targeted campaigns will set themselves up well for the rest of the holiday shopping season."
1...Frasers Group, whose brands include Sports Direct, House of Fraser, and Flannels, reports that Antrim in Northern Ireland has become the first of its warehouses to go live with a Microsoft Dynamics 365 warehouse management system (WMS).
In a LinkedIn post, Jakob Vestergaard, Product Manager - Warehouse at Frasers Group, said: "Two years of work. One major milestone. We're live. As the first warehouse in the group to adopt D365 WMS, Antrim marks an important milestone in our wider warehouse transformation journey."
"Over the last few years, Frasers Group has invested heavily in elevating our stores. This programme is about taking the next step by elevating the warehouse operations that power them, creating a more scalable, visible and consistent platform to support our stores, brands and customers. This achievement would not have been possible without the dedication of teams across the business and our partners."
He concluded: "Go live is a major achievement, but it isn't the end of the story. Over the coming months we'll continue working with our warehouse teams, Microsoft, Binary and InterRadish to refine the solution, introduce additional capabilities and build out the global warehouse template that will support future warehouse deployments across Frasers Group. This is the first step in a much bigger journey. Looking forward to what comes next."
