2026 RTIH Innovation Awards RFID Project of the Year finalists include Checkpoint Systems and RADAR
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards RFID Project of the Year category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 RFID Project of the Year finalists as follows:
Checkpoint Systems and JD Sports
JD Sports is transforming inventory management across its European estate using RFID technology. Following a 2024 pilot with Checkpoint Systems, RFID was deployed to over 400 UK and Ireland stores during 2025, with the remaining 680 European stores targeted by October 2026.
Checkpoint’s ItemOptix software provides them with real-time inventory visibility, improving stock accuracy, shelf replenishment and product availability while enabling more advanced, data-driven retail operations for the future. RFID is also being extended across JD Sports’ European distribution centres, combining ItemOptix software with RFID tunnel technology to improve inventory visibility throughout their supply chain.
Edgbaston and Levy
The Edgbaston RFID Smart Cup System transformed the management of reusable cups during the 2026 cricket season. Replacing a legacy deposit refund process with RFID enabled cup validation, the solution ensured deposits could only be refunded when a genuine deposit backed cup was scanned.
Alongside improving financial controls, the system enhanced cup return performance, reduced cup losses, lowered staffing requirements and delivered a more efficient returns operation across major sporting events. The project combined RFID technology, automated validation and operational process redesign to create a scalable circular economy solution. Across the first full season, the system achieved a 95.7% cup return rate, improved deposit integrity and generated significant labour and security savings, demonstrating both commercial and sustainability benefits.
Lager 157 and ClarityRFID
Lager 157, a Swedish fashion retailer, has partnered with ClarityRFID to pilot the Clarity Store solution across three stores in Denmark, Sweden and Finland.
Over three months, the pilot replaced manual stock counting and shipment receiving with real-time, item level RFID data, lifting stock accuracy to as high as 98-99.8% and SKU accuracy to as high as 97% in participating stores.
For a retailer built on product, price and word of mouth trust rather than traditional marketing, that level of inventory visibility strengthens the promise at the centre of the brand: knowing exactly what's in stock, in which size and colour, at which store. Lager 157 and ClarityRFID are now working toward a full production roll-out across the retailer's six-country store network, planned for 2027.
RADAR
RADAR lays claim to being the only vertically integrated provider of overhead RFID, delivering perpetual, item level inventory intelligence for retail at scale.
Through item detection and location sensing today, and expanding user behavior analytics over time, RADAR gives retailers the ability to measure their physical stores the way they already measure their ecommerce business, turning one accurate inventory foundation into a different advantage for every function of the business.
As of Q3 2026, RADAR is deployed across more than 1,700 stores and 21 million square feet of retail space, indexing over 55 million products and processing more than 130 billion tag reads daily.

2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Retail Media Technology finalists include Hanshow, Jisp, and Lloyds
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Retail Media Technology category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Retail Media Innovation finalists as follows:
Age-Gate by Adello
Age-Gate by Adello places a camera-based age check inside a mobile ad unit, so age restricted advertising is shown only after the viewer's age has been checked.
The facial age estimate runs on the user's own device, and no image is stored or transferred. In a two-week live campaign in Switzerland's tobacco category in May 2026, using a deliberately generic creative, the unit delivered 67,801 impressions at 63.5% viewability and 1.1 minutes average dwell time. 25.6% of users who engaged completed the age check. Switzerland's revised tobacco law, expected in early 2027, requires age controls for online tobacco advertising.
FashSYNC
FashSYNC is an in-store retail media platform delivering real-time SKU level intent detection and closed loop attribution on Samsung digital out-of-home (DOOH) displays. It is unlocking a $22-30 billion untapped retail media market in premium fashion, where grocery retail media dominates (Cooler Screens) but fashion has remained fragmented and undermonetised.
Hanshow
Hanshow, shopreme and Lucky Cart have created a unified smart cart ecosystem that brings personalised, measurable retail media into the physical shopping journey. Hanshow provides the connected hardware and in-store technology foundation, shopreme delivers the smart cart software, self-scanning experience and store integration, while Lucky Cart contributes its personalisation and retail media capabilities.
Together, the solution transforms the shopping cart into an intelligent touchpoint supporting product discovery, relevant offers, basket visibility and faster checkout. Already deployed with a leading European grocery retailer, it demonstrates how physical stores can combine digital convenience, shopper first engagement and new retail media opportunities through one scalable platform.
Jisp
Jisp's Scan & Win Video platform turned McVitie's Moments packaging into an always on shopper engagement channel for long-standing FMCG partner Pladis.
Using Scan & Win’s new video technology to allow the scanning of a physical product to start entry (not on-pack QR), instant win mechanics and multi-channel marketing, the six-week campaign generated over 1,000 product scans from 132 unique shoppers, with 62% returning to scan more than once, a new benchmark for the platform.
Paid social reached over 137,000 consumers at a 3% click-through rate, while owned channels drove more than 5,400 landing page visits. Beyond engagement, the campaign delivered valuable first-party shopper data for Pladis.
Lloyds Rewards
Lloyds Rewards is one of the UK's largest bank led retail media platforms. Connecting over ten million eligible customers with retailers, brands and partner propositions through Lloyds' digital channels. Over the past year, Lloyds has evolved Rewards beyond traditional cashback, introducing challenges, prize draws, retailer discounts and strategic partnerships to create multiple ways for brands to engage customers.
Particular Audience and Intersport Austria
Particular Audience and Intersport Austria have put relevance at the centre of on-site retail media. Instead of letting bids alone decide what shoppers see, Particular Audience's AI ranks sponsored and organic results together, so ads stay useful to the shopper.
In the first five weeks the programme delivered 536,653 impressions, 6,988 clicks and a 1.30% click-through rate at a 17.2% cost of sale. Brand halo ROAS reached 17.3x against 5.81x on SKU last click, McKINLEY and Active Rebel brand sales rose 28.6% and 28.5%, and a Bayesian A/B test showed a 100% probability of beating control.

items.title: Budget is a 'critical test' for John Healey as high street grapples with rising costs and 'fragile' confidence
items.summary: With John Healey facing crunch talks with industry bosses on Downing Street this morning, the British Retail Consortium (BRC) warned further tax hikes would push up prices and cost jobs.
items.body:
Budget is a 'critical test' for John Healey as high street grapples with rising costs and 'fragile' confidence
The Chancellor has been warned he faces a 'critical test' in the Budget as the High Street grapples with rising costs and 'fragile' confidence.
With John Healey facing crunch talks with industry bosses on Downing Street this morning, the British Retail Consortium (BRC) warned further tax hikes would push up prices and cost jobs.
And it said retail sales rose by just 1.3 per cent in the year to September - far slower than the 2.3 per cent increase seen 12 months earlier.
'The Chancellor cannot promise to ease the cost of living while piling more costs onto the retailers working to keep prices down,' said BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson.
'With confidence fragile, this Budget is a critical test. Retailers will do everything they can to protect value for customers, but Government must play its part.
'Another rise in business rates would push up pressure on prices, choke off high-street investment and put local jobs at risk.
Retailers have urged the Chancellor not to pile the sector with further tax rises at the Budget
'This Budget must back retail to invest, employ and grow - not make it harder.'
The comments came after Marks & Spencer chief executive Stuart Machin urged Healey to 'to get Britain growing again by taking the handcuffs off business' in the Budget on October 28.
Writing in the Daily Mail on Saturday, Machin branded Labour's previous two efforts under Rachel Reeves 'a disaster' and said: 'At the very least, he should start unravelling the mistakes of the last two Budgets.'
The Chancellor will hold talks with retail and hospitality chiefs at 11 Downing Street today.
Representatives from businesses and trade groups including the Co-op, the British Beauty Council and UK Hospitality are expected at the breakfast meeting.
Retailers have cited the high cost of employment - related to inflation-busting rises in the minimum wage and a surprise increase to National insurance contributions for firms - as a major headache.
The war in the Middle East has also driven up the costs such as ingredients and energy.
Large retailers have been particularly concerned that Andy Burnham's promise to cut business rates for pubs, clubs and music venues will be funded by hitting supermarkets with a so-called 'warehouse tax'.
But it was reported over the weekend that this was not in Healey's plans for the Budget.
Small businesses are also calling for help, however, with industry groups calling for thousands of firms to be excluded from paying business rates altogether.
The Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) said raising a key threshold that gives firms business rates relief from £12,000 to £25,000 would help unlock growth by removing 250,000 small firms from the levy.
Tina McKenzie, FSB's national chairman, said: 'Small businesses across the UK are up against huge and persistent cost rises that are seeing so many struggle with running their business, let alone investing and expanding. This is the most important opportunity for the Government to make its more pro-small business tone a reality.
'If we are to get the growth needed, the Budget must be a moment for some meaningful action, backing the small firms and self employed that are so crucial to the economy.
'We need a tax system that rewards ambition rather than punishes it.'

items.body:
Tech for Retail 2026 preview: retail leaders and technology innovators set to meet in Paris
Tech for Retail will return to Paris on 30th November and 1st December, bringing together more than 420 exhibitors, 15,000 retail decision-makers and over 200 conferences at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles. For its sixth edition, the European retail technology show will place artificial intelligence, omnichannel commerce, supply chain transformation, data and the augmented store at the heart of its programme.
A strong international line-up will complement a French retail perspective, with senior executives from across Europe and global retail organisations taking to the Main Stage.
AI, innovation and the future of retail
The event will open on 30th November with Alexandre Bompard, Chairman and CEO at Carrefour, setting the tone for two days focused on the technologies reshaping the retail industry. He will be followed by Delphine Viguier-Hovasse, L’Oréal’s Chief Innovation & Prospective Officer, Artefact CEO and founder Vincent Luciani, and Bernard Osta, CEO at second-hand fashion marketplace Vestiaire Collective.
AI will be a recurring theme throughout the programme, moving beyond experimentation towards practical applications across retail operations, customer experience and commerce. Sessions will explore how technology can deliver measurable impact, from product data and personalisation to new approaches to customer engagement.
The luxury and beauty sectors will also feature prominently. A dedicated session, The Reinvention of Luxury through Technology, will bring together Nathalie Cabut from L’Oréal, Elise Ducret from Carita and Pascale Miguet from Publicis Luxe to discuss how technology is changing the luxury experience.
A truly European perspective
International speakers will bring a broader perspective to the conversations around retail transformation.
On 1st December, Mikko Kärkkäinen, Group CEO and Co-Founder at Finnish retail technology company RELEX Solutions, will open the second day with a keynote focused on supply chain and logistics. His appearance reflects the growing importance of technology in forecasting, planning and building more agile retail operations.
The programme will also feature Nadine Graf, President Europe, UK & Ireland & Emerging Markets at The Estée Lauder Companies, and Michelle Lamberti, Chief Omnicommerce Officer at ADEO. Their sessions will add an international dimension to discussions around beauty, customer journeys and the convergence of physical and digital commerce.
Food retail will have a strong presence too. Martín Tolcachir, CEO at Grupo DIA, Fredy El Hakim, IT Procurement Manager at Mercadona, and Nacho Gonzalez Hernandez, CEO and Board Member at Spanish retail association AECOC, will discuss how technology can move from innovation to practical, scalable impact.
From the augmented store to sustainable retail
The programme will look beyond AI alone, reflecting the increasingly interconnected challenges facing retailers. A session on the augmented store will examine the balance between retail media, digitalisation and energy efficiency, with Miguel Ángel González Gisbert from Carrefour, Sébastien Fourcy from Vusion and Marc Taieb from Wifirst. Other sessions will address sustainability, circular economy, regulation, recommerce and new revenue models.
The show will also explore the evolution of product data as a strategic asset, the role of AI in content and merchandising, and the impact of technology on European marketplaces and omnichannel strategies.
Alongside the conference programme, Tech for Retail will offer visitors access to more than 420 exhibitors and 75+ startups, as well as thematic guided tours designed to help retailers identify relevant technologies and solutions. The event will also host Innovation, AI, Customer Experience and Startup Awards, highlighting technologies and companies shaping the next phase of retail.
With senior retail executives, technology providers and international speakers gathered under one roof, Tech for Retail 2026 will offer a European view of how technology is moving from experimentation to implementation, and how retailers can turn innovation into tangible business value.

Fellow conference session panellists from L’Oréal and Wolf & Badger, a marketplace that champions independent fashion and homeware, emphasised how important good data tagging, quality, and hygiene is amid a digital revolution where AI agents can buy on behalf of consumers.
According to Matt Berzinski, EMEA Field CTO at Ping Identity, who was also on the panel entitled ‘The new online storefront - unlocking the next phase of agentic commerce’ on 6th October: “AI agents are inherently lazy, so if you’re too hard to find they will just move on.” Having good data mastery is therefore more important than it has ever been.
“It is also up to us to identify agents and control them,” he added, as the conference session panel moved on to discuss the centrality of good governance and know your agent (KYA) compliance. This could become as vital as customer (KYC) compliance requirements in the future. “Trust is crucial in this coming era where the ability to know who is a human, who is an agent, and to have appropriate verification is key.”
GEO
Aside from security internally and with ecosystem partners, data mastery is also vital for the Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) future that will displace traditional SEO in search in the future. The skill of structuring and tailoring online content so that AI large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT and Gemini, can find and recommend your brand will be crucial in driving future sales.
As Othman Bennis, Chief Digital and Marketing Officer, L’Oréal Europe, said: “L’Oréal is moving to having 18-20 data fields to hundreds in the future in terms of our product attributes. This is necessary for the agentic AI future.” He also shared that his firm is working with OpenAI now that they’ve opened an ad function on ChatGPT.
Early days
George Graham, CEO at Wolf & Badger, noted that his firm was the first in Europe to take an agentic AI initiated order. “We are already transacting,” he said, while stressing it is very early days in the migration to agentic commerce. “We use Stripe’s agentic commerce suite of tools and work with Meta to enable our offering.”
Pricing pressure
In regard to the potential pricing pressure from AI agents searching out better deals for their humans, using economies-of-scale negotiating tactics depending on their number of adherents, Rithum’s Hall thought this likely. “LLMs will tend to direct you to the cheapest price. However, I personally don’t just shop on price, so there is still room for retailers to differentiate themselves.”
According to Wolf & Badger’s Graham fundamentally they’re still a retailer that needs to curate their offering to achieve the best products on their platform, the best service, loyalty and retention, at the best price they can get. This means delivering: Good CX; Products, price and service; Fulfilment. “These are always at the core of good retailing,” he said. “The fundamentals don’t change.”
L’Oréal Europe’s Bennis agreed, although he did stress his company is not complacent about the coming revolution and is already working with Alibaba and Amazon among others to protect discoverability. “Ultimately though, it is the one with the best CX that will win this race.”
There is no doubting that the race is underway. “Don’t leave too many data gaps and you’ll be OK,” he reassured attendees, while stressing that if you do then the agent might get it wrong when classifying your brand. “Don’t give them the chance. Don’t put your brand out there with a terrible dataset.”
It appears that data really is the ‘new oil’ in the coming agentic AI era where it will grease the modern economy in the way petrol did the 20th century. Retailers need to be ready for the coming revolution.
Q&A
In response to questioning from RTIH, the participants said they weren’t worried about the possibility of AI agents sifting through data that had already been sifted by other agents.
The virgin internet, where human checked and verified information can be mined and interrogated, is fast becoming a thing of the past. But this wasn’t a worry to the panellists, or at least it’s outside of their control and parameters. Verification against inaccuracies or fakes is also a potential countermeasure.
“Even if you’re training on synthetic data that has been artificially created, retailers will still have their own data control mechanisms and procedures,” said Wolf & Badger’s Graham. Rithum’s Hall, meanwhile, advised retailers in the room to just concentrate on what they can control and to get that right.

items.body:
Ikea flagship store brings home furnishing products to Douyin E-commerce shoppers across China
Ingka Group has launched an Ikea Douyin official flagship store in China. The new digital touchpoint will offer more than 6,500 Ikea products across 179 categories, with delivery available in 301 cities across China.
The move brings the retailer in to the short-form video and content commerce platform (a sister platform to TikTok under ByteDance). The store will complement its existing stores, website, app, WeChat and other e-commerce channels in China.
Lydia Song, Ikea China Acting CEO and President and CSO, says: “People in China are increasingly moving between inspiration, discovery and shopping in ways that are highly connected and increasingly digital. Douyin E-commerce gives us an opportunity to meet people in a new context, learn what resonates with them and make Ikea more accessible to more people. This is not simply about adding another sales channel. It is about understanding how we can become part of people’s everyday lives in new and relevant ways.”
Parag Parekh, Chief Digital Officer at Ikea Retail (Ingka Group), pictured below, comments: “Retail is increasingly about being present wherever and whenever people want to meet us, while making those experiences feel like one connected Ikea. What is particularly interesting about new platforms like Douyin E-commerce is the opportunity to learn. They help us understand how inspiration, interaction and commerce are coming closer together, and what that could mean for how we continue to develop the Ikea omnichannel experience.”

Virgin Money backs British retail technology company Snappy Group with new funding facility boost
Scottish retail technology firm Snappy Group has secured a new funding facility with Virgin Money’s Venture Debt team. The exact amount of which was not revealed, although it is said to be a seven figure deal. Best known for its quick commerce marketplace, Snappy Shopper, Snappy Group has evolved into a broader retail technology platform, providing marketplace, order aggregation, white label and retail media solutions to retailers across the UK.
Barry McGonagle, Chief Financial Officer at Snappy Group, pictured below, says: “We are delighted to secure this facility with Virgin Money at such an important moment for Snappy. Demand for our products and services is growing rapidly, transaction volumes across the platform are at record levels, and the market opportunity in front of us is significant.”
“This facility adds further firepower alongside previous equity investments and gives us the capital and flexibility to accelerate into that opportunity with confidence. We have known the team at Virgin Money for several years and are pleased to be partnering with them as we enter this next phase of growth.”
Andrew Stirrat, Senior Director of Venture Debt at Virgin Money, says: “We have closely tracked Snappy Shopper’s progress over several years and have been consistently impressed by the strength of the business and its sustained growth. We are delighted to support one of Scotland’s leading scale-up technology companies through this lending facility and look forward to backing the next phase of its ambitious expansion.”
Snappy Group works with a number of independent and national retail partners across the UK convenience sector, including SPAR, One Stop, Morrisons and Co-op.

items.title: Cyber attack scare for H&M: Fashion giant probes claims it was targeted by same group that hacked JLR
items.summary: The Swedish fashion giant is looking into a potential cybersecurity incident made by a group called Shinyhunters. It follows a cyberattack on Asos last week.
items.body:
Cyber attack scare for H&M: Fashion giant probes claims it was targeted by same group that hacked JLR
H&M is investigating claims it was targeted by a cybercriminal last week.
The Swedish fashion giant is looking into a potential cybersecurity incident made by a group called Shinyhunters. It follows a cyberattack on Asos last week.
Shinyhunters previously claimed it was behind a major cyber attack on Jaguar Land Rover last summer, along with other hacking groups known as Scattered Spider and Lapsus.
It had also reportedly demanded around £400,000 in a ransom payment to prevent data being sold after attacking Ticketmaster in 2024.
An H&M Group spokesman said: ‘We are aware of the claims circulating online regarding a potential cybersecurity incident involving a limited scope of H&M Group data.
‘Protecting the security of our systems and data is of utmost importance to us.’
Swedish fashion giant H&M is looking into a potential cybersecurity incident made by a group called Shinyhunters
She added: ‘We are currently investigating these claims to assess their validity and so far we have no indication that our data environment has been compromised.
‘We take any potential threat to our systems and data seriously and as this work is ongoing, we are unable to provide further details at this time.’
The H&M group, which has 4,000 stores in more than 80 markets, has a roster of fashion and homeware brands including Cos, Weekday, & Other Stories and Arket.

items.title: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
items.summary: Hundreds of stores were targeted by the overnight hack, which spoiled fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.
items.body:
Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
- Published
Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyber attack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.
Hackers reportedly gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight.
The chief executive of CoopÃ©rative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the "extremely serious and unprecedented" attack.
More than 100 of the chain's supermarkets were targeted, while at least 300 stores from IntermarchÃ© and its Netto brand were affected, according to the AFP news agency.
IntermarchÃ© said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported.
Some supermarket staff reportedly said they were hit by waves of hot air when they opened freezer units on Monday morning.
French broadcaster BFMTV published an image showing a freezer in an ice cream aisle displaying a temperature of 26.5C.
Two supermarkets in the Alsace region reported losses of â¬270,000 (Â£228,000) between them, the broadcaster added, meaning the nationwide total could run into the millions.
The Paris prosecutor's office told AFP it had opened an investigation into the incident, which it called a "large-scale cyber-attack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France".
Eoropean Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen condemned the hack in a post on X and added: "Food security requires more attention at all levels. Because the weaponisation of food has become a reality."
The full scale of the attack is so far unclear.
Reports in specialist retail and local media said stores from other food giants, including Carrefour, E.Leclerc and Monoprix, were also attacked. BBC News has approached the supermarket chains for comment.
In a post on X, CoopÃ©rative chief executive Dominique Schelcher said staff were "fully mobilised, in co-ordination with refrigeration specialists, to restore the situation as quickly as possible".
He called for an investigation into the hack and said targeting equipment essential to the French food supply was "unacceptable".

items.title: One Stop invests in franchise growth with online delivery rollout
items.summary: One Stop is providing all franchise partners with access to its order aggregation solution, helping stores simplify operations, improve efficiency, and maximise online sales opportunities. The convenience retailer said its franchise partners already benefit from competitive commission rates and a fully managed online delivery solution,… This story continues at One Stop invests in franchise growth with online delivery rollout Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The convenience retailer said its franchise partners already benefit from competitive commission rates and a fully managed online delivery solution, so, it’s latest investment forms part of One Stop’s ongoing commitment to provide partners with the tools, technology and support they need to grow their businesses and unlock new revenue opportunities.
By introducing the solution across more than 240 franchise stores this autumn through Deliverect technology, it enables franchise partners to manage orders from Deliveroo, Just Eat, Uber Eats and Snappy Shopper.
Instead of switching between different devices and platforms, stores can now process, manage, and fulfil all incoming orders through a single device.
The solution also introduces a standardised picking process, which, said One Stop, helps to simplify operations, reduce errors, cut staff training requirements, and lower picking costs.
Tim Josephs, head of online at One Stop, said: “Online delivery continues to create significant growth opportunities for independent retailers.
“By providing our franchise partners with access to a proven and successful order aggregation solution, we’re helping them improve operational efficiency by simplifying the day-to-day management of online orders, while also providing actionable business insights via our state-of-the-art dashboard.
“The solution gives stores greater visibility of their performance, enabling them to identify sales trends, uncover growth opportunities and make more informed business decisions. Best of all, we’re protecting franchisees’ margins by covering all monthly integration fees.”
The platform also supports improved stock management and product scanning functionality, helping stores reduce refund claims.
Raj Sangha, a One Stop franchise partner whose Erdington store was among the first to trial the solution, said: “The biggest benefit for us has been simplicity. Managing online orders across different delivery platforms used to be time-consuming, but having everything brought together in one system has transformed our day-to-day operations.
“It has improved efficiency for colleagues and made a noticeable difference to the overall customer experience.”
One Stop has provided dedicated onboarding support and guidance to help stores maximise the benefits of the platform.

items.title: Malibu targets RTD category with new Punch range
items.summary: Malibu is launching Malibu Punch, a new range of 10% ABV canned cocktails designed for a new generation of adult consumers. Available in Watermelon Punch, Peach Tea Punch and Piña Colada Punch, the range combines fruit flavours with the signature Caribbean spirit of Malibu. Created… This story continues at Malibu targets RTD category with new Punch range Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Available in Watermelon Punch, Peach Tea Punch and Piña Colada Punch, the range combines fruit flavours with the signature Caribbean spirit of Malibu.
Created for higher-energy social occasions, from pre-drinks and house parties to festivals and spontaneous get-togethers, Malibu Punch expands the brand’s RTD portfolio.
The launch forms part of the broader ambition of Malibu to accelerate growth within the evolving RTD category and strengthen relevance with younger adult consumers.
Liam Murphy, marketing director, Pernod Ricard UK Ricard, commented: “Malibu is already a ready-to-drink super brand in the UK having helped to establish the category more than a decade ago.
The onus is on us to innovate and deliver against evolving consumer trends. Malibu Punch is a bold 10% ABV proposition created specifically for pre-drinks, parties and spontaneous get-togethers.
“With three distinctive flavours and significant investment behind the launch, we believe Malibu Punch can recruit a new generation of adult consumers, build on Malibu’s distinct credentials and bring further excitement and value to the fast-growing RTD category.”
Malibu Punch will be supported through the broader “Do Whatever Tastes Good” campaign platform, with activity designed to drive awareness, trial and recruitment among adult consumers.
Malibu Punch is available now, with an RRP of £3.50 per 237ml can.
